question: Can adaptive movement-completion detection replace the FIXED 1.5s post-roll without losing contact/follow-through/recovery?
method: Replay on gold events (n=5, all bench cases): trigger = target wrist-speed peak inside the labeled event; FIXED = trigger+1500ms; ADAPTIVE v2 = first of (a) SETTLE: wrist speed < max(0.15, 25% peak) sustained 400ms, (b) NEXT-STROKE VALLEY: dip <60% peak then rise ≥1.5× valley → end at valley, (c) hard safety max trigger+2500ms. Truth: labeled eventEnd + phase followThroughEnd/recoveryEnd.

results.perEvent: 3/5 dramatically better (dink 1060→160, rally2 869→70, vic 1051→251 recovery excess); 2/5 never settle (continuous rally exchanges) → safety max (+1s trailing, still loss-free)

findings: ADAPTIVE v2 halves end error and cuts recovery-end excess 76% while producing slightly SHORTER clips — accuracy and latency improve together.

v1 (settle-only) LOST to FIXED (median 1750 vs 1080): in continuous play the athlete never settles. The next-stroke-valley condition is what makes adaptive viable — completion and multi-event segmentation are the same problem.

The 2 never-settled cases are rapid volley exchanges; wrist-speed valleys between hits were too shallow for the 1.5× rise gate. Session-mode event chaining will need paddle/contact confirmation, as the event-decoupling plan already states.
decision: NOT PROMOTED to Swift yet. n=5, replay-only, trigger idealized (label-window peak, not the live rising-edge trigger). The shipped FIXED 1.5s stays. Promotion path: instrument the live trigger timestamps, re-run this bench with real trigger times on ≥20 gold events, then gate like D-027.
